user.title: Electric Fence
user.description: Electric Fence records failed and successful logins and who changed settings. It never affects logins. Select submit to set it up with the default settings.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Electric Fence is already set up. Only one instance is allowed.

collector_disabled.title: Electric Fence collector disabled
collector_disabled.description: Electric Fence turned off the {collector} collector because Home Assistant no longer behaves as expected: {reason}. Logins are not affected. Please report this at the Electric Fence issue tracker.

storage_error.title: Electric Fence cannot write to its database
storage_error.description: Electric Fence could not write to its database: {error}. Logins are not affected, but new records are being dropped until this is fixed.

ip_ban_disabled.title: Home Assistant IP bans are switched off
ip_ban_disabled.description: Electric Fence bans addresses through Home Assistant's own IP ban, which is switched off, so Electric Fence cannot block any address. To switch it on, go to Settings > System > Network > HTTP server > IP banning, turn on Enable IP banning, and save. Saving restarts Home Assistant. Logins are not affected.

schema_too_new.title: Electric Fence database is from a newer version
schema_too_new.description: The Electric Fence database uses schema version {version}, but this version of Electric Fence supports up to {supported}. It was probably written by a newer Electric Fence. Electric Fence did not load and left the database unchanged. Update Electric Fence to that newer version. Logins are not affected.

integration_files_changed.title: Files of {name} were changed
integration_files_changed.description: The installed files of the custom integration {name} differ from its published copy or from the copy Electric Fence recorded: {files}. If you didn't change them, someone else may have. Reinstall {name} from its source to restore its files. Home Assistant is not affected otherwise.

integration_archived.title: {name} is archived
integration_archived.description: The author of the custom integration {name} archived its repository, so it gets no more updates, including security fixes. Consider replacing it with an integration that is still maintained.

integration_unmaintained.title: {name} has not been updated in a long time
integration_unmaintained.description: The custom integration {name} has had no update in more than {months} months, so it may no longer get security fixes. Check whether it is still maintained, or replace it.

ban_limit_reached.title: Electric Fence reached its limit of active bans
ban_limit_reached.description: Electric Fence has {limit} active bans, the most it keeps, so it is not banning more addresses. This usually means an attack from very many addresses. Failed logins are still recorded and usernames under attack are still slowed down. Check the Bans tab in the Electric Fence panel. This message goes away once bans expire or are lifted.

init.title: Electric Fence settings
init.description: IP geolocation by DB-IP ({dbip_url}) when DB-IP Lite is selected. Changes apply immediately. Shortening the history retention deletes older records right away. This machine, the Supervisor and trusted proxies are never banned or slowed down; other local addresses are, unless you exempt them under Bans.

data.mask_ips: Mask IP addresses in the panel

data_description.retention_days: Days of history to keep, from 1 to 3650.
data_description.geoip_provider: Where country lookups come from. DB-IP Lite needs no account. MaxMind GeoLite2 needs an account ID and license key.
data_description.reverse_dns: Look up host names for IP addresses.
data_description.record_values: Store what each setting was and what it became. Passwords, secrets, tokens, keys and coordinates are always hidden. Turning this off also removes the values already stored.
data_description.mask_ips: Show only the start of each IP address (203.x.x.x, 2001:db8:x:x:x:x:x:x) and hide host names and the address of the Home Assistant a browser logged in through in the Electric Fence panel, for example for screenshots. Full addresses are still recorded, and notifications and the logbook are unchanged.

bans.name: Bans
bans.description: Block an IP address after repeated failed logins.

data.exempt_local: Never ban or slow down local addresses

data_description.auto_ban: Ban an IP address that fails too many logins.
data_description.ban_threshold: Failed logins from one address (for IPv6, one prefix) before it is banned, from 1 to 100.
data_description.ban_window_minutes: The period in which the failed logins are counted, from 1 to 1440 minutes.
data_description.ban_hours: How long a ban lasts, up to 8760 hours. 0 means the ban never expires.
data_description.ban_repeat_offenders: Double the ban for each further ban of the same address within 30 days. The fourth is permanent.
data_description.ipv6_prefix: IPv6 failures are counted, and bans enforced, per prefix of this length, from 48 to 128. One IPv6 host usually holds a whole /64, so it can't escape a ban by changing address. 128 counts single addresses.
data_description.exempt_local: Off by default: a compromised device on your network, or a Tailscale peer, is treated like any other address. Turn on to exempt LAN, Docker, Tailscale and other local addresses, as earlier versions did. Loopback, the Supervisor and trusted proxies are always exempt. If Home Assistant runs in Docker without host networking, every device on your network may share one address; turn this on there.

username_protection.name: Username protection
username_protection.description: Detect one username being guessed from many addresses and slow those logins down.

data_description.username_protection: Treat many failures against one username from several addresses as an attack.
data_description.attack_threshold: Failed logins against one username, from 2 to 1000.
data_description.attack_min_ips: Different addresses the failures must come from, from 1 to 100.
data_description.attack_window_minutes: The period in which the failures are counted, from 1 to 1440 minutes.

notifications.name: Notifications
notifications.description: Choose which events send a message. Turning one off stops only the message; events, the panel and the audit log are unaffected.

data_description.notify_failed_login: Create a persistent notification when a login fails.
data_description.ha_login_notification: Replace dismisses Home Assistant's own login notification, but only while failed login notifications are on.
data_description.notify_ip_banned: Send a message when an address is banned.
data_description.notify_username_attack: Send a message when a username is being guessed from many addresses.
data_description.notify_new_country: Send a message when someone logs in from a country not seen before.
data_description.notify_ban_ended: Send a message when a ban expires or is lifted.
data_description.notify_targets: Notify entities, such as phones, that also receive these messages.

integration_checks.name: Integration checks
integration_checks.description: Check installed integrations for changed files and for integrations that are no longer maintained.

data_description.verify_files: Compare installed integration files with the official copy.
data_description.integration_repairs: Raise a repair when a check finds a problem.
data_description.unmaintained_months: Months without a release before an integration counts as unmaintained, from 1 to 36.
data_description.scan_delay_minutes: Minutes to wait after startup before the first scan, from 1 to 1440.
data_description.ignored_files: One file per line: the integration folder, a slash, then the path inside it, for example my_integration/data.json.

forwarding.name: Log forwarding
forwarding.description: Send events to a syslog collector or SIEM. Forwarding never affects logins.

data_description.forward_enabled: Send each event to the collector as a syslog message.
data_description.forward_host: Host name or IP address of the collector.
data_description.forward_port: Port of the collector, from 1 to 65535.
data_description.forward_protocol: Wazuh's own syslog listener accepts TCP and UDP. Use TLS only with a collector that supports it, such as rsyslog.
data_description.forward_verify_tls: Check the collector's certificate when using TLS.
data_description.forward_ca_pem: Optional PEM text of the certificate authority that signed the collector's certificate.

maxmind.title: MaxMind GeoLite2 credentials
maxmind.description: Enter your MaxMind account ID and license key. They are checked with MaxMind before saving.

data_description.maxmind_account_id: The account ID shown in your MaxMind account.
data_description.maxmind_license_key: A license key created in your MaxMind account. It is stored in the config entry and not shown again.

error.invalid_maxmind_credentials: MaxMind rejected the account ID or license key.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach MaxMind. Check the connection and try again.
error.forward_host_required: Enter a host to forward events to.
error.forward_ca_invalid: The CA certificate is not valid PEM text.

options.replace: Replace it with Electric Fence's notification
